title: ONCO-SCAN: Detection of Pediatric Cancers at Birth
summary:
Cancer is one of the leading causes of death in childhood. To date, there have been few options for prevention and early detection. However, genetic and epigenetic changes can occur years before a clinical diagnosis is made and could potentially be used for early detection.

The study therefore investigates whether pediatric cancers can be detected at birth using circulating DNA from dried blood spots. To this end, genetic and epigenetic characteristics in dried blood spots from women who later developed cancer are compared with those of control subjects. In addition to tumor detection, the study examines tumor classification, hereditary cancer predispositions, and the mapping of tumor heterogeneity. The goal is to lay the groundwork for potential newborn cancer screening and earlier diagnosis and treatment of pediatric cancers.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of dried blood spots from patients diagnosed with cancer during childhood or adolescence.
Retrospective analysis of dried blood spots from children and adolescents without a diagnosed malignancy serving as controls.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients diagnosed with cancer during childhood or adolescence
- Written consent from the participant and/or a legal guardian to participate in the study
- Siblings of a participant in the patient cohort or children diagnosed with a cancer predisposition syndrome who have not developed a tumor at the time of study enrollment
Exclusion criteria:
No written consent from the participant and/or a legal guardian to participate in the study
